subject: Quantatek AWS — Proposal for 3-year prepaid commitment & ramp options
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Mikhailova <elena.mikhailova@quantatek.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quantatek AWS — Proposal for 3-year prepaid commitment & ramp options

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really appreciate the context on expected usage across the first 18 months. As promised, I wanted to put a concise set of commercial options on the table for a Marketplace-based private offer (AWS) so your procurement team can review quickly. High level: we can support either annual prepay invoices or a single multi-year prepaid commitment on the Marketplace private offer path. Differences are mostly around discount depth and billing/cost recognition on your side.

Proposed options (ballpark):
- Option 1 — 1yr annual prepay: 12% discount on list with annual upfront payment; renewal at same list unless we agree a scale-based uplift.
- Option 2 — 2yr prepaid (paid upfront via Marketplace private offer): 18% total discount; billing handled as a single private-offer charge; we can issue contractor-friendly language for amortization.
- Option 3 — 3yr prepaid (paid upfront via Marketplace private offer): 25% total discount; includes explicit ramp schedule (see below) and an annual usage true-up for unforeseeable overage.

Ramp suggestion for Option 3 (example):
- Yr1 commit: 40% of ARR estimated usage
- Yr2 commit: 75%
- Yr3 commit: 100%
We’re happy to adjust those percentages if you expect a different growth curve.

Operational notes:
- Marketplace private offer is the cleanest route for AWS procurement to provide a single PO that drives the private-offer charge. We can supply the private offer ID and the DocuSign-ready term sheet.
- For accounting: if you need amortization-friendly language, we can provide a seller attestation and suggested treatment language — many customers amortize over the contracted period.
- Taxes/marketplace fees: marketplace transaction fees and tax passthrough follow AWS standard flows; we can provide a sample invoice showing pass-through line items.

Next steps I suggest: send me the procurement contact (or feel free to cc procurement@quantatek.com) and confirm whether you prefer: (A) annual prepay billing, (B) a single multi-year private-offer prepay, or (C) want a two-step (1yr to start with option to prepay the remaining 2yrs at a fixed price). I’ll loop in finance and legal as needed and push a private-offer draft.

I’ve attached a short term sheet and a draft private-offer template for quick review.

Thanks —
Rafael
Head of Cloud Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A few quick procurement questions so we can scope internally:
1) For the 3yr prepaid option, is the entire payment captured by AWS Marketplace at contract execution (i.e., we issue one PO to AWS and the charge occurs up front) or do you support an annual invoicing split while keeping the private offer (i.e., private offer but Redwood invoices us annually)?

3) We need to confirm whether the private offer route will be treated as an ELA-equivalent for our legal team — specifically, do you allow custom termination clauses and 3rd-party addenda in the private-offer terms, or must we accept the marketplace baseline?

Looping in our procurement (procurement@quantatek.com) and Michael Chen (mchen@quantatek.com) who handles vendor accounting.

Elena / procurement team,

Thanks for the questions — answers inline below and I’ve added Lauren (legal) and Stephanie (finance) to scope the contract/billing details.

1) Payment capture on AWS Marketplace: for a private offer we can do either:
   - Single upfront charge captured by AWS at execution (typical for a full-prepay private offer), or
   - We can create a private offer and separately invoice you annually (less common; adds manual reconciliation).
   If procurement needs spend spread across fiscal years for accounting, the second option can be arranged; however, the deeper discounts we’re showing are tied to full upfront prepayment via Marketplace private offer.

2) Support SLA credits during ramp: SLA credits are pro rata to the service tier purchased. During Yr1 ramp (if you buy the 3yr with the proposed ramp percentages) credits apply to the committed tier; usage over commit would be true-up, and support credit calculations follow the effective tier for each month. Stephanie, can you confirm the exact credit calculation model (cc’d).

3) Legal flexibility on private offer: Marketplace private offers do allow redlines in the accompanying seller terms, but the overall commercial acceptance is governed by AWS's private-offer flow. Lauren, I’ll hand this to you to propose acceptable early-termination/buy-down language that aligns with marketplace constraints.

Attached: updated term sheet (with the three options) and a draft private-offer payload for AWS.

Rafael

Hi Elena / procurement team,

Thanks for raising the legal items — below are clarifications and a proposed minimal set of buy-down / termination terms designed to be Marketplace-friendly while protecting both parties:

- Private-offer mechanics: AWS will accept a single PO and collect the full charge for an upfront prepaid private offer. The seller terms we provide sit alongside the AWS private-offer acceptance; we can include a short addendum that governs amortization and buy-down rights.
- Early termination / buy-down: proposed: buyer may request a buy-down with 90 days written notice; buy-down price = remaining contract value less 20% administrative adjustment; exceptions: insolvency or material breach.
- Ramp schedule: include explicit percentages per contract year; any usage shortfall triggers a one-time reconciliation true-up at contract anniversary, unless parties agree otherwise.
- Data/security: we will include SOC 2 Type II attestation and KMS/HSM integration notes; these are standard and we can provide the SOC report under NDA.

I’ve attached a two-page legal summary and a DocuSign-ready term sheet we can send for signature once commercial terms are agreed. If procurement has specific PO language (net-30, net-45, PO reference fields) please share — that drives how we populate the private offer metadata for AWS.

Lauren Bishop
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
